title: Flying Dragon
text: “Information manipulation? Ah… If I remember correctly, in the future storyline, they started a war to take over the world, right? So maybe they spread false information—like saying Takt had won and asking people to come celebrate—and then rounded them all up in one fell swoop… or something like that?”
“I don’t know the details.”

“Even if I’m right, that tactic won’t work anymore… the remnants have already escaped… So that leaves us with either hunting down and eliminating each of the fugitives one by one, or forcing them to give up their quest for revenge.”

This has become quite a hassle. If that’s the case, it means the public execution my future Father carried out was, for better or worse, necessary after all. With so many remnants running rampant right now, I understand that all too painfully.
“In the end, the only option is to win the war and then prove our innocence. We have to make the world know that Takt was the villain…”
“If my Father gives the order, I, Motoyasu, will destroy any country.”
“Yeah. I know, but only to the extent that you don’t interfere too much… That said, will the Hero have to join the war between Siltvelt and Shieldfreeden?”
Lost in deep thought, my Father turned to face me.
“…Motoyasu-kun.”
“Yes?”
“In the future, if something happens that causes us to loop back, I want you to remember the current situation absolutely clearly so we don’t repeat the same mistakes…”
“Understood.”
“And if possible—so that war can be avoided and my knowledge of the future can be put to good use… that’s right. I want you to avoid war as much as possible, just like I did in the future.”
My Father bowed his head to me with strong determination. Understood. I, Motoyasu, will do my best to prevent war should we ever find ourselves in a loop, for the sake of my Father’s request.
However, I can’t imagine how my Father from the future managed to avoid the war. Well… I’ll just have to think it through as best I can.
“Father, I, Motoyasu, have etched your words into my memory.”
“I’m counting on you.”
And so, as we talked, we continued our journey to wipe out the remaining rebels.
After taking down the pigs that appeared while I was giving a speech revealing Takt’s true identity, we returned to Siltvelt Castle.
“We’re back now. What’s the situation with the Shieldfreeden Army?”
Father returned to the castle and addressed the representative of the Shusaku clan. The representative replied to his words.
“Currently, the Shieldfreeden Army is advancing from the south. Due to aerial bombardment and gunfire—though we’re extremely dissatisfied—our country is being pushed back.”
“I’m pretty sure firearms and such in this world depend on Lv, right? So, aren’t the people flying those planes high-Lv?”
“Probably…”

“According to the information about the future I heard from Motoyasu, I don’t really understand how they managed to neutralize the airplanes. Apparently, that king of Melromarc suppressed them through strategic maneuvering.”
“So if a wise and enlightened king appears, it’s easy to neutralize those airplanes… B-but that wise and enlightened king is our enemy.”
“I see… That’s true. It’s not something we can just imitate. By the way, have you figured out the whereabouts of the Seven Star Weapons of the Claw and the Seven Star Weapons of the Whip?”

The story goes that when we took down Takt, the Seven Star Weapons he was carrying were unleashed by the flash of Brionac. According to those who were watching the airship from outside, a ball of light flew into the sky from the glow of my Brionac. I do recognize that light itself—after all, it flew from the sky toward Midori. I don’t know if it took residence in someone or if it fell somewhere.
“We’ve confirmed its location. It was enshrined in our nation’s sacred precinct.”
“Sacred precinct?”
“It’s a deep forest near my castle. The Seven Star Weapons of Tsume were enshrined there.”
“I see… In that case, we’ll have to declare to a nation—or something—that can verify this, that there are two Seven Star Weapons in existence and that we have no intention of monopolizing them.”
“We’ve already done so. However… it seems Takt actually possessed three Seven Star Weapons.”
“Three!? That means one hero other than the Hero of Tsume has already been sacrificed, right?”
“Yes.”

That was quick. It seems Takt has already killed one hero who was summoned by a Seven Star Weapon at this stage. According to Siltvelt, the Four Holy Weapons were summoned first, so they must have been sacrificed not long after being summoned.
“Faubrey is currently planning to dispatch an investigation team to our country, but…”
“It’s doubtful whether we can trust that investigation team, isn’t it?”
“Yes… After all, Faubrey is the country Takt belonged to. Even though they claim to be impartial, they can’t ignore the presence of remnants under Takt’s influence.”
“We’re starting to hit a dead end… I suppose. We can only hope there’s someone over there with some common sense.”
“Yes. There are reports that people under Takt’s influence are active in Faubrey as well, so they’re in a state of confusion too.”
“Either way, we have to get through this. Let’s do our best to prove our country’s innocence!”
“Yes, sir! I’m truly sorry that it seems unlikely we’ll be able to fulfill the Shield Hero’s wish.”
“Don’t worry about it for now… We’re already in this together.”
“Thank you for the Shield Hero’s mercy.”
My Father is responding to the Shusaku representative, who salutes him with mixed feelings. On the way here, my Father muttered to himself.
“…This conflict might have been caused by my coming to this country. Takt is the root of the problem, but unless I handle this more… skillfully, the damage will only keep mounting.”

I’ve committed those words firmly to memory. While it’s true that Takt is the root of the problem, killing him without careful consideration leads to situations like this. If we were to loop again, we’d have to think carefully about the circumstances under which we kill him.
“For now, what we have to do is deal with the airships from Shieldfreeden…”
Father began poring over a map at the operations headquarters, deep in thought.
“The people of this country have tried fighting the airships using flying dragons and Beastmen who can fly, but it’s difficult… Well, then, there’s only one thing left to do.”
Father looked over at me.

Facing the battlefield, Father laid out his strategy. Up until now, Filolial-sama’s troops, led by Yuki-chan and the others, had carried us this far. However, the moment I heard Father’s plan, I blurted out without thinking:
“I absolutely refuse!”
Father’s plan sent a chill down my spine, and hives broke out all over my body.
“Be patient, Motoyasu-kun. There’s no other effective strategy!”
“I still don’t want to do it!”
I touched the feathers on Yuki-chan’s back to escape from that unpleasant reality.
“Ah, Motoyasu-sama… I’d love for you to pet me some more.”
“Ahaha—include Kou too—pet me too!”
“I, Yuki, will gather everyone and use Ceremonial Magic to shoot that plane down!”
Yuki-chan stepped forward and offered her suggestion.
“I thought about that, too. But they say the plane’s flying too high and going too fast, so it’s hard to hit it with Ceremonial Magic. That’s why the surest way is for Motoyasu-kun to do his best.”
“But—”
“I’m sorry, Yuki-chan, but I want you to understand. If we’re going to minimize the damage even a little… we have no choice but to have Motoyasu-kun do it.”

Ugh… My father-in-law is desperately trying to persuade Yuki-chan, who’s throwing a tantrum. I respect him deeply and am absolutely determined to obey his orders, but this time, what Father has ordered is something I really want to refuse. If I were to do something like that, this Motoyasu would have hives for several days. And it might even leave scars.
“I… understand. Father’s orders are absolute…”
“Lord Motoyasu! You mustn’t do anything so reckless!”
“This, too, is ultimately for your sake, Father. I, Motoyasu, will ensure this operation succeeds no matter what.”
“Yeah… It pains me too, but I’m asking you to do this… I should be the one doing this myself, but since all I can do is protect you, you’re free to resent me for it.”

I can sense the anguish behind my Father’s decision. I understand. I understand the thoughtfulness behind his placing his trust in me, Motoyasu. Even if I’m tormented by pain, I, Motoyasu, will accomplish this difficult mission.
“Alright, let’s move out.”
“Yes, sir!”

We salute and begin preparing for deployment alongside Father. A high-pitched screech and the sound of shrapnel can be heard from above. Looking up at the sky, I see airplanes circling and bombing the battlefield and nearby towns. First, we must shoot down those planes.
